title: Implement plan-ladder decision A: outsideLadder lowcode consequence (five locales) and contract §2.4 capability-matrix boundary
goal: Land the implementation follow-up that the signed W7 decision A reserved for a standalone small PR: the operator-facing consequence (the outsideLadder warning does not name the hidden lowcode surfaces) and the contract-side statement of the capability-matrix boundary (builtin four tiers only; custom code = quota bucket + free capability tier; gating is UX-only). Zero logic, schema, route or permission changes; normalizeTenantPlan fail-closed semantics untouched per the decision's design constraint.
findings: W7 decision A (2026-10-28, maintainer-delegated) reserved its implementation as a follow-up L1 PR: outsideLadder consequence sentence in five locales plus contract/design-doc boundary wording.

Premise correction recorded by this packet: the decision doc §1 claims the warning 'only says not-in-ladder, not the price', but the copy in place since #427 (2026-10-25) already separates capabilities-at-free from quotas-still-apply. The real delta is naming the lowcode gated surfaces.

The decision doc's '设计文档 §2.4 相邻处' does not exist: MULTI_TENANT_DESIGN.md is a vision document with no plan/capability section and defers to the contract. The normative boundary paragraph therefore lands in the contract §2.4 the decision itself cites as its anchor.
TenantPlanMatrix already renders custom codes as free (the call site passes normalizeTenantPlan's normalized value), so decision item 3 is confirmation-only.

implementationNotes: The five locales carry the same sentence as equivalent translations, not independent wording; no page enumeration (generator/wizard/widget) to avoid copy that rots as gating consumers evolve.

The contract paragraph must keep three statements apart: quotas still apply from the table row, capabilities resolve to free (fail-closed normalization), and gating is UX-only (hiding neither grants nor revokes permissions; authorization stays with the §2.3/§3 permission chain). The decision's 'newly introduced failure mode' (operators mistaking quota rollback) is prevented by exactly this split.
V1.9 is a Clarification: no invariant, error code, In/Out edge or write-side behaviour changes, so the §8 contract-change gate flow is not triggered; the §9 version row keeps it traceable.

No new test asserts the copy (grep confirms nothing pins the old string); the regression sensor for locale parity is audit:i18n-locales, and consistency with the matrix is guaranteed by the existing normalized call site.
